in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Thank you for reaching out! I'll help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To start, I need to know about the child or children you're asking about:

**How old is your child?** (This determines the basic eligibility pathway)

- Under 16 years old
- Between 16 and 19 years old
- 20 years old or over

Please let me know the age of the child you're claiming for.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll continue the assessment based on your situation profile. Let me work through this for Alex, who is 9 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check an important requirement. **Do you normally live in the UK?**

This is a key eligibility requirement. If you don't normally live in the UK, there are some special circumstances that might still qualify you, such as:
- Having settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Being a Crown servant working abroad
- Living in certain qualifying countries

Could you tell me about your current living situation?

conversation.text:
I've completed the assessment based on your circumstances. Unfortunately, I need to provide you with the outcome:

---

## **Child Benefit Eligibility Assessment Result**

**Result: NOT ELIGIBLE**

**Reason:** You do not meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit.

### Why this decision was reached:

For Alex (age 9):
- ✓ Alex is under 16 years old (qualifying age)
- ✓ Alex is not working 24+ hours per week
- ✓ Alex is not receiving qualifying benefits in their own right
- ✓ Alex has not started a disqualifying apprenticeship
- ✗ **You do not normally live in the UK** - This is the deciding factor

### What this means:

To claim Child Benefit, you must normally live in the UK. If you don't live in the UK, you might still qualify if you meet special circumstances such as:

- Having **settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Having **pre-settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme AND meeting additional requirements (working, studying with sufficient resources, or being a jobseeker)
- Being a **Crown servant** working abroad
- Living in certain qualifying countries

### Next Steps:

If you believe you might meet one of the special circumstances listed above, you can contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office for clarification:
- Phone: 0300 200 3100
- Website: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit

If your circumstances change and you move to the UK or meet one of the special residency conditions, you may become eligible at that time.

---
